title: Al-Sharaa Declines to Attend G7 Summit Despite Historic Invitation
detail: Despite an invitation hand-delivered to Finance Minister Mohammed Yisr Barnieh during G7 financial talks in Paris — which would have marked Syria's first-ever participation in a G7 summit since its founding in 1975 — President Ahmad al-Sharaa did not attend the 52nd G7 Summit held June 15–17 in Évian-les-Bains, France. Syrian officials gave no public explanation for the decision. The summit had been expected to showcase Syria's bid to position itself as a Middle East transit hub amid the ongoing Strait of Hormuz shipping crisis. Analysts noted the episode illustrates the limits of Syria's rapid diplomatic normalization even as sanctions relief and bilateral engagement accelerate elsewhere.

media.caption: Al-Sharaa ultimately did not attend the G7 summit in Évian despite a hand-delivered invitation

title: US Envoy Barrack Meets SDF's Abdi and KRG's Barzani in Erbil on Military Integration
detail: US Special Presidential Envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack met Kurdistan Region President Nechirvan Barzani and SDF Commander-in-Chief Mazloum Abdi in Erbil on June 16, 2026, to discuss the operational steps required to integrate the SDF and the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (AANES) into Syrian state and military institutions. Barrack reaffirmed Washington's commitment to supporting the integration process, which stems from the January 30, 2026 SDF-Damascus agreement, and reportedly conveyed US expectations for the process to be completed by the end of 2026.

media.caption: Nechirvan Barzani, Tom Barrack, and Mazloum Abdi meet in Erbil to discuss SDF integration, June 16, 2026
